question: Which credential does an identity provider present to provision users into an organization (a long-lived bearer token held by whom, with what expiry and rotation), which identity attribute (userName, external id or subject) is the stable key of a provisioned person, what does a deprovision do (suspend, archive or delete the membership), which provider groups may confer which organization role, and who may read the provisioning log?
decision: Use per-org scoped and revocable SCIM credentials in protected secret storage (prefer short-lived credential rotation, maximum 90 days for bearer tokens), bind stable identities to provider issuer plus externalId, and verify organization/configuration. Deprovision immediately suspends membership and revokes session, roles, mandates, external grants and device tokens; preserve auditable historical records. IdP groups can grant at most member/steward under approved mapping; org admins see redacted provisioning logs.
originalProposedDecision: SCIM authenticates with a per-org bearer token from scim_configurations (expiry at most 1 year, rotatable by admins). Stable key: the provider's externalId. Deprovision suspends the membership. Groups may confer only member or steward. Provisioning log: org admins.
